Definition: {properly, to spoil (literally, by breaking to pieces); figuratively, to make (or be) good for nothing, i.e. bad (physically, socially or morally)}
BiblicalUsage: The fourth kingdom shall be strong as iron, for iron breaketh in pieces and subdueth all things, and as iron that breaketh all these, so shall it break in pieces and bruise.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the iron kingdom's strength is real but borrowed, and the stone cut without hands will break it in turn.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
